verdict.root_cause: productcatalogservice is originating the errors itself. In every errored trace the deepest error-flagged span is its own GetProduct handler, with all flagged ancestors being callers (frontend, checkoutservice) [tr_fa36d7823d16]. Failure is conditional: only GetProduct calls that make a FeatureFlagService/GetFlag child call fail, while sibling GetProduct calls without that child and ListProducts calls in the same traces succeed, and the GetFlag child spans are themselves unflagged [tr_fa36d7823d16]. Errors return promptly (0.7-2.0ms), not via timeout or exhaustion, and are new against an exactly-zero 30-minute baseline with a change point at 10:58:45 [tr_529e7ceb35de, tr_fa36d7823d16]. The consistent mechanism is a feature-flag value governing the GetProduct path set to a failure-injecting state: reading the wrong value is what breaks the request.
verdict.reasoning: Causal direction comes from the traces: the error flag terminates at productcatalogservice's GetProduct span and every flagged ancestor is a caller, which explains frontend and loadgenerator alerting as consumers [tr_fa36d7823d16]. Downstream origins were excluded on the same trace set - featureflagservice GetFlag children unflagged, cartservice clean and a sibling not a callee, adservice absent from the path, checkoutservice flagged only on ancestors [tr_fa36d7823d16]. Latency/timeout is excluded because errored spans finish under 2ms while the only slow path carries no error flags; exhaustion is implausible because failures partition cleanly by whether the flag lookup occurred rather than by load [tr_fa36d7823d16, tr_529e7ceb35de]. What remains is a value-driven branch, which is bad_config in the strict sense, so the fix is reverting the flag value rather than a restart or artifact rollback. Change-log queries found nothing for this service but covered only onset-forward time, so they neither support nor exclude a pre-onset flip [tr_8b7434752206].
open_questions: No log line was ever retrieved: both log queries used a hyphenated label that does not index this service's stream, so the flag name and error text are unverified [tr_f3528a2a9096, tr_4dd8bf8248eb].
The pre-onset change window was never queried, and featureflagservice's own change history and current flag values were never examined [tr_0a067fef7256, tr_8b7434752206].
The two metric baselines disagree (zero 30-minute baseline vs. pre-existing bursty errors over 6 hours), and no latency or saturation series were returned at all [tr_529e7ceb35de, tr_b06b351638e9].

alternatives.root_cause: A deploy or code change to productcatalogservice introduced a fault on the flag-consulting GetProduct branch.
alternatives.why_not: No deploy record exists in the onset-forward window, and the failure's clean partition by flag-lookup presence points to a value being read rather than a changed artifact - though the pre-onset window was never checked [tr_8b7434752206, tr_fa36d7823d16].

alternatives.root_cause: featureflagservice returns a malformed or unexpected flag payload that productcatalogservice cannot handle, making the defect a dependency behaviour rather than a wrong stored value.
alternatives.why_not: Indistinguishable from the primary verdict on trace shape alone, but the error flag stops at productcatalogservice and GetFlag spans are clean, so the failing decision is made in productcatalogservice [tr_fa36d7823d16].

proposal.expected_effect: No action proposed, so no effect is predicted. The reason: the only action whose class matches the verdict (revert_config on productcatalogservice) fails both of its stated preconditions. The change log for productcatalogservice returned a well-formed empty result over the whole queried window, so no prior configuration is recorded for this service to restore [tr_0a067fef7256, tr_8b7434752206], and no evidence on the board names a configuration or flag change inside the incident window — the change-history result explicitly rules out a recorded flag flip or config edit for this service [tr_0a067fef7256]. The flag-value mechanism the verdict describes lives in FeatureFlagService, whose GetFlag child spans are unflagged and whose own change history and current values were never examined [tr_fa36d7823d16]; featureflagservice is not in the blast radius this brief permits as a target, so the value that would actually need reverting is outside what this system may touch. rollback_image is also unavailable on its precondition (no prior image tag and no deploy named in the window) [tr_0a067fef7256], restart_service is wrong on mechanism (the failure is conditional on a specific code path taking a flag lookup, not process state) [tr_fa36d7823d16], and scale_service is unavailable in this world.
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if any of the following is produced: (a) a change-history query over the window *preceding* 10:58:45 — never run, per [tr_0a067fef7256, tr_8b7434752206] — that returns a config or flag entry for productcatalogservice with a recorded prior value, which would satisfy revert_config's preconditions directly; (b) a change-history query against featureflagservice showing a flag flip near 10:58:45, which would name the correct target and make the scope question, not the evidence question, the blocker; (c) a Loki query using the unhyphenated service label that returns productcatalogservice error lines naming a flag and error text, since both existing log queries used a selector that indexes nothing [tr_f3528a2a9096, tr_4dd8bf8248eb]. Any one of those turns abstention into a concrete proposal.
proposal.risk: The risk of abstaining is that a live conditional failure keeps burning GetProduct calls on the flag path — roughly 1% of requests on average with bursts near 9% [tr_529e7ceb35de] — for as long as it takes to run the three missing queries. That is real user-visible harm on the frontend and checkout paths. I accept it because the alternative is recreating productcatalogservice with a configuration nobody has read: the change log has no prior config for this service to restore [tr_0a067fef7256, tr_8b7434752206], so 'revert' would either be a no-op that costs a container recreate and buys a false all-clear, or would install whatever default the tooling considers previous — potentially changing dependency addresses and moving traffic, on a service that is currently serving the large majority of its requests successfully [tr_b06b351638e9].
proposal.blast_radius: No change, so nobody sees anything. Had revert_config been proposed on productcatalogservice, the recreate would reset connections for its named callers — frontend and checkoutservice, both of which appear as error-flagged ancestors in these traces [tr_fa36d7823d16] — plus recommendationservice, which the brief lists as reached from productcatalogservice; loadgenerator would register the resulting request failures. The continuing cost of inaction is carried by those same callers.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical multi-service alerting starting at productcatalogservice with frontend following 30s later suggests a real downstream failure propagating upward, not a quiet world. No open incidents to attribute it to, and the alerts alone do not distinguish a bad deploy from resource exhaustion in productcatalogservice.
